title: Terraform orchestration wrapper for Dedicated pool create/expand (idempotent + retries)
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Context
We need a single, repeatable way for the provisioning pipeline (fleet-provisioner) to create and expand Dedicated pools across regions/SKUs. Today operators run ad-hoc terraform apply steps and reconcile outputs by hand; this creates inconsistent naming, missing outputs, and non-deterministic retries.

Goal
Add a Terraform orchestration wrapper that:
- Runs terraform plan/apply for Dedicated pool infra (new pool + expansion).
- Is idempotent: re-running with the same desired spec should converge without duplicating resources.
- Has safe retry semantics: transient errors auto-retry; non-transient errors fail fast with actionable classification.
- Defines a stable contract for required inputs + outputs consumed by later stages (imaging/bootstrap/validation + control-plane registration).

Non-goals
- Re-architecting the terraform modules themselves (handled in redwood-terraform PRs), beyond adding/standardizing outputs we need for the wrapper contract.
- Replacing procurement/quota processes.

Proposed shape
Wrapper component: fleet-provisioner (service) invokes terraform via a runner abstraction.
- Interface supports dry-run (plan only) and apply.
- State backend + locking: remote state (S3/Dynamo or Terraform Cloud equivalent) with per-pool workspace; enforce lock acquisition and set a max lock wait.
- Correlation: every terraform run is tied to provisioning run_id (from ENG-2742 state machine) and emits structured events (ENG-2748).

Idempotency rules
- Workspaces are keyed by {env}/{region}/{pool_id}.
- Apply inputs are derived from a canonical PoolSpec (control plane) -> terraform variables. This conversion must be deterministic.
- Use standardized resource naming tags/labels so a rerun finds the same resources.
- Treat "expand" as updating a desired_size / nodegroup count variable in-place; no resource recreation unless inputs change (e.g., GPU SKU change is disallowed; must be a new pool).

Retry semantics
- Retry eligible:
  - Cloud provider transient API errors (5xx, throttling, request timeout)
  - Terraform provider timeouts
  - State lock contention (bounded)
- Non-retry (fail fast):
  - Invalid input/spec (schema violations, missing required vars)
  - Permission denied / IAM policy issues
  - Quota exhausted (unless we explicitly mark as "retry after quota approval")
- Backoff: exponential with jitter; cap total retry window to 30m for terraform stage (stage budget aligned with time-to-ready).
- Always safe to retry: wrapper must detect partial apply and continue the same workspace with the same desired spec.

Inputs (contract)
Required inputs to run terraform:
- env: staging | prod
- pool_id: control plane pool identifier
- region: e.g., us-east-1 / eu-west-1 (must match terraform module supported regions)
- gpu_sku: e.g., a100-80g / h100-80g (string value used for module selection/vars)
- desired_capacity: integer (target GPU nodes or nodegroups; clarify based on module)
- network_profile: reference (CIDRs/subnets profile id) OR explicit vpc/subnet ids depending on env
- module_version: pinned ref (git sha or semver tag) for the terraform modules
- tags: customer_id, pool_name, cost_center, owner
- run_id: provisioning run correlation id
Optional inputs:
- allow_destroy: false by default (guardrail)
- apply_timeout_minutes
- max_retries
- dry_run: boolean

Outputs (contract)
Wrapper must return a stable output payload to downstream stages:
- workspace_id (or state key)
- terraform_run_id
- applied_module_version
- vpc_id
- subnet_ids
- security_group_ids
- cluster_name
- cluster_endpoint
- cluster_ca_bundle_ref (pointer to secret store / artifact location)
- nodegroup_ids (or ASG ids depending on provider)
- instance_profile_arn / iam_role_arns (if needed for bootstrap)
- logs_url (where to find terraform stdout/stderr)
- output_fingerprint (hash of outputs to support drift detection later)

Implementation notes
- The wrapper should call terraform with explicit -lock-timeout and capture detailed logs.
- Use a small error classifier to map terraform/provider errors into: TRANSIENT, QUOTA, PERMISSION, INVALID_SPEC, UNKNOWN.
- Emit stage timing: plan_start/plan_end/apply_start/apply_end and failure classification.
- Ensure no secrets are logged (sanitize env vars; redact provider creds).

Acceptance criteria
- Can create a new Dedicated pool in staging end-to-end through terraform stage with a single API call from fleet-provisioner.
- Can expand an existing pool by increasing desired_capacity; rerun does not create duplicate resources.
- Retries demonstrated in staging by injecting a transient failure (throttle/timeout) and observing successful convergence.
- Contract documented in ticket + referenced in Confluence overview; downstream stages can rely on standardized outputs.
- On failure, operator receives a clear error category + link to terraform logs.

Links
- Linear umbrella: ENG-2741
- State machine: ENG-2742
- Structured events/metrics: ENG-2748
- Terraform module refactor PRs (expected dependency): redwood-terraform PR-913 / PR-914

Open questions
- Do we standardize on "desired GPU nodes" vs "desired nodegroups" as the capacity variable? (Recommend nodes; modules can map internally.)
- State backend ownership: do we reuse existing redwood-terraform remote state buckets or create dedicated fleet-provisioner workspaces?
- How do we handle quota failures: retry with backoff vs fail and surface as "Blocked: quota" with operator action required?
comments: 2024-02-21 — Nina Petrova: For capacity variable: please keep wrapper input as desired_gpu_nodes and let terraform map to ASG/nodegroup counts per SKU/region. Avoid leaking provider-specific constructs into control plane.

2024-02-22 — Miles Thornton: +1 on explicit error classification. Also please include lock wait metrics; we’ve seen long lock contention when two operators try to expand the same pool during an incident.

2024-02-23 — Rafael Mendes: SRE ask: ensure wrapper never auto-destroys on retry. We had a historical case where a failed apply led to a manual taint/destroy and we lost auditability. Guardrail should require allow_destroy=true + admin only.

2024-02-27 — Gabe Wilson: Drafted interface in fleet-provisioner: ApplyPoolInfra(PoolSpec, moduleRef, dryRun) -> (TerraformResult). Added workspace key format env/region/pool_id and lock-timeout=10m. Next: wire error classifier + retries.

2024-03-01 — Keiko Yamamoto: Please make sure regional defaults are applied before terraform invocation (tags, IAM role naming, subnet selection). Otherwise we’ll keep re-learning the same region-specific footguns.

2024-03-05 — Gabe Wilson: Integrated with redwood-terraform standardized outputs (vpc_id, subnet_ids, security_group_ids, cluster_name/endpoint). Added output_fingerprint hash for later drift detection. Retrying only on TRANSIENT/LOCK; QUOTA fails with actionable message and sets provisioning stage to Blocked.

2024-03-08 — Vanessa Ortiz: Reviewed contract section—looks good. Please add logs_url to result so operators can jump straight from control plane run page to terraform output without spelunking runner pods.

2024-03-12 — Gabe Wilson: Added logs_url + run_id propagation into terraform runner labels. Observed idempotent rerun in staging (same PoolSpec) produces no diff on plan and exits cleanly. Injected throttling -> retry succeeded on attempt 3.
2024-03-18 — Vanessa Ortiz: Marking Done. Follow-ups captured in ENG-2754 (drift detection) and ENG-2750 (operator CLI).
